transcript: In Japan, a country of disasters, preparing for earthquakes and typhoons that may come at any time is indispensable. Strengthening buildings and preparing evacuation plans have become standard responsibilities for national and local governments. Preparation at home is also important. Emergency food, water, flashlights, a well-maintained portable radio. Keep these in an accessible place Children must be taught how to behave when an earthquake strikes First drop, cover your head And hold on under a sturdy desk After the shaking stops, turn off flames If it is safe to do so So that you do not evacuate barefoot Keep shoes by the bedside Deciding where the family will gather is also important If people are scattered at school, workplace and home, where will you meet? If this is not decided in the initial stage, you may be unable to contact one another in the confusion. As a mental preparation for disasters, there is a concept called normalcy bias. People want to think I will be fine Even when a heavy rain evacuation order is issued They think it's still fine And fail to escape in time To overcome this Accept that if nothing happens That is good And evacuate early Take actions that you hope will prove unnecessary That instinct saves lives Disaster preparation is a matter of planning and habit The accumulation of small daily preparations Becomes a great difference When the moment comes better safe than sorry This old proverb remains an unchanged truth

segments.text: In Japan, a country of disasters, preparing for earthquakes and typhoons that may come at any time is indispensable.
Strengthening buildings and preparing evacuation plans have become standard responsibilities for national and local governments.
Preparation at home is also important.
Emergency food, water, flashlights, a well-maintained portable radio.
Keep these in an accessible place
Children must be taught how to behave when an earthquake strikes
First drop, cover your head
And hold on under a sturdy desk
After the shaking stops, turn off flames
If it is safe to do so
So that you do not evacuate barefoot
Keep shoes by the bedside
Deciding where the family will gather is also important
If people are scattered at school, workplace and home, where will you meet?
If this is not decided in the initial stage, you may be unable to contact one another in the confusion.
As a mental preparation for disasters, there is a concept called normalcy bias.
People want to think I will be fine
Even when a heavy rain evacuation order is issued
They think it's still fine
And fail to escape in time
To overcome this
Accept that if nothing happens
That is good
And evacuate early
Take actions that you hope will prove unnecessary
That instinct saves lives
Disaster preparation is a matter of planning and habit
The accumulation of small daily preparations
Becomes a great difference
When the moment comes better safe than sorry
This old proverb remains an unchanged truth
